subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser-specific public URL/domain/path denylist or warnlist, or fold this into a broader cross-tool egress/security policy?
rationale: The requested feature would become operator-facing navigation security/config surface, and related open issues show competing scopes that automation should not choose without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Design browser policy first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser deny/warn behavior for navigation, redirects, proxy-routed profiles, defaults, and docs before implementation.

options.title: Make egress policy canonical
options.body: Use the broader egress tracker as the product direction if maintainers want one policy for browser, web_fetch, web_search, and plugin HTTP egress.

options.title: Decline browser-specific surface
options.body: Close or narrow this if maintainers decide known bot-blocked public domains should remain an operator workflow concern outside OpenClaw config.

recommendation.title: Design browser policy first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define browser deny/warn behavior for navigation, redirects, proxy-routed profiles, defaults, and docs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history signal across browser CDP/SSRF and shared network-guard policy work adjacent to this decision.
